corrected_verdict: KNOWN for the product and power neurons at every 2<=b<=nu. The per-frequency AM-GM/Parseval budget is Hoff 2017 Lemma 2 in Fourier form, via Gunasekar et al. 2018 Lemma 7. That covers b=2, including the observation that a neuron can carry several frequencies at no extra cost. At b=nu it is Morwani App. F.1 for n=2 and Li et al. Lemmas D.7-D.8 for all n. For 2<b<nu it follows in one line from monotonicity of l_q quasi-norms. The power-neuron bound is an equality: C_b^{nu/b} = n! B_p exactly. The ReLU bound C_2 <= p^{-n}/2 is FALSE for n>=2. The correct bound from the same argument is C_2 <= 1/(2p), independent of n. It is novel in application but elementary.
issues:
I re-fetched and re-read both of the checker's confirmed citations, and both are accurate.
- Morwani et al. 2311.07568 (ICLR 2024 spotlight per the arXiv comments): App. F.1, "Proofs for cyclic groups (Theorem 7)", eqs. (6)-(9), pp. 25-26. The steps are Plancherel, then "inequality of quadratic and geometric means", then Cauchy-Schwarz with ||z||_2 <= ||z||_1 <= p/2, giving sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)). Lemma 18 is on p. 36. The checker's "eqs (6)-(9)" is right; call the location "App. F.1" rather than "the appendix".
- Li et al.: PMLR 258:523-531 (AISTATS 2025), confirmed on proceedings.mlr.press/v258/li25b.html. Lemma D.7 (eq. 15, coefficient k!) and Lemma D.8 (value 2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2})) are as the checker describes. The refs.bib entry for li2025nsum lacks series, volume and pages, and the key is still cited nowhere in the sections (only a TODO at intro.tex:22).

Where the checker's verdict fails:

(1) Missed prior art (math lens), Gunasekar, Lee, Soudry, Srebro, NeurIPS 2018 (arXiv 1806.00468).
- Lemma 3: for full-width circular convolutions, beta^ = diag(w^_1)...diag(w^_{L-1}) w^_L.
- Lemma 7: min_{w:Pconv(w)=beta} ||w||_2^2 = L ||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}. The proof in App. D, eq. (85), is per-coordinate AM-GM.
- Our product neuron's coefficient beta_j = 2p^{-nu} prod_t u^_t(j) conj(w^(j)) is the same Hadamard product of nu DFTs. So our C_2 statement, with equality for balanced neurons carrying any number of frequencies, is Gunasekar Lemma 7 with L=nu, up to normalisation and the pairing of j with -j.
- The checker called the "several frequencies at no extra cost" observation new. It is not.
- The origin of the step is Hoff, CSDA 115 (2017) 186-198, Lemma 2 (Sec. 3.1): the l_{2/K} penalty equals the minimum of the sum of squared L_2 norms over Hadamard factorisations, with the minimum at balanced factors.
- With these, "B_p is independent of b" is a one-line corollary: C_b <= C_2^{b/2} by l_q monotonicity, and the single-frequency cosine attains it for every b.

(2) The ReLU bound is wrong. The checker recommended keeping it as ours.
- Appendix l.283 claims sum_{j in F}|h^(j..j) w^(j)| <= (p/4)||omega||^2, hence C_2 <= p^{-n}/2.
- With the paper's unnormalised DFT on Z_p^n: sum_{k!=0}|h^(k)|^2 = p^{2n} Var(h) <= p^{2n-1} sum_t ||u_t||^2.
- The same Cauchy-Schwarz then gives (p^n/4)||omega||^2, so C_2 <= 1/(2p). This equals B_p at nu=2 and does not depend on n.
- Numerical counterexample (verify_relu_c2.py): at n=2 the cosine ReLU neuron gives 1.262e-2 vs the claimed 1.020e-2 (p=7), 8.13e-3 vs 4.13e-3 (p=11), and 6.89e-3 vs 2.96e-3 (p=13). It scales as ~0.09/p. At n=3, random neurons give 4.19e-4 vs 3.76e-4 (p=11) and 2.96e-4 vs 2.28e-4 (p=13). All values stay below 1/(2p).
- The qualitative use (Theorem universal plus the flat Gamma_1 maximiser applying to ReLU) survives. Any stated constant must become 1/(2p), giving gamma*_2 <= 1/(2(p-1)).
- I found no precedent for a ReLU per-neuron margin budget. Mohamadi et al. (ICML 2024, 2407.12332) is l_inf and quadratic only; He et al. 2602.16849 has no norm budget. My search coverage is limited: the WebSearch quota was exhausted, and Semantic Scholar and the arXiv API returned 429 or empty results. I relied on direct arXiv fetches and HF paper search.

(3) The power-neuron "<=" should be "=".
- beta_pow = n! beta_prod holds identically for every omega (max error 3e-16 in verify_power_neuron.py).
- The cosine witness attains n! B_p at b in {2, 2.5, nu} for n=2 and n=3.
- The checker suggested this only tentatively. It is correct.

extra_citations.why: Lemma 3: in the Fourier basis, a linear circular-convolution network is a Hadamard product of the layers' DFTs. Lemma 7 (Sec. 5; proof in App. D, eq. (85), by AM-GM): min ||w||_2^2 = L ||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}. Our product neuron's beta_j is a Hadamard product of nu DFTs, so our b=2 budget C_2 is this lemma with L=nu, including the equality for neurons carrying several frequencies. Cite it at approach.tex l.54-58 and at the b=2 remark in app:models. The venue is taken from the PDF footer ('32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2018)'); page numbers were not fetched.

Lemma 2 (Sec. 3.1, arXiv 1611.00040): with q=2/K, the penalty lambda||beta||_q^q equals the minimum over factorisations u_1 o ... o u_K = beta of lambda(sum_k u_k^T u_k)/K, attained when |u_{k,j}| is constant in k. This is our per-frequency AM-GM step (the balanced-factor equality case), stated in coordinates. It is the classical source for the identity 'l_2 cost on K multiplicative factors = l_{2/K} quasi-norm'. Metadata confirmed via Crossref.
